chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says at the end of the Fajr prayer and at the end of the Maghrib prayer, seven times: 'In the Name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is neither might nor strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent', Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will repel from him seventy types of afflictions, the easiest of which is the wind (hurricane), vitiligo, and insanity. And if he was wretched, his wretchedness will be erased, and he will be written among the fortunate.

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might nor strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' seven times after Fajr and Maghrib prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the transformative power of dhikr in shifting one's spiritual state from wretchedness to fortune, a concept deeply rooted in Shia devotional practice. The promise of protection from seventy types of afflictions highlights the comprehensive nature of divine mercy, covering both physical ailments like leprosy and mental states like insanity, as well as existential destiny. This practice serves as a daily spiritual anchor, reinforcing reliance on God's power and greatness after the pivotal prayers of dawn and evening.
